title: Train a byte-pair encoder, then encode and decode
brief: Write the pair counter, the merger, and the training loop, then replay the learned merges to encode text and join bytes to decode it.
hints: get_pair_counts walks each inner list on its own: for a, b in zip(tokens, tokens[1:]): counts[(a, b)] = counts.get((a, b), 0) + 1. A word with the pair twice adds 2.
merge_pair scans with a while loop. On a match write new_id and move on by two, otherwise write the current id and move on by one. That is why [5, 5, 5] becomes [20, 5].

train_bpe splits with _pretokenize, turns each piece into a list of bytes, and loops while 256 + len(merges) < vocab_size. Pick the winner with min(counts, key=lambda p: (-counts[p], p)), store vocab[256 + i] = vocab[a] + vocab[b], then merge. Stop when get_pair_counts returns an empty dict.
apply_merges_to_word starts from ids = list(word_bytes). For each i, pair in enumerate(merges), call merge_pair([ids], pair, 256 + i) and keep the first list it returns.
encode loops over _pretokenize(text), turns each piece into list(piece.encode('utf-8')), replays the merges on it, and extends one flat list.
decode is b''.join(vocab[i] for i in ids).decode('utf-8'). Decoding one id at a time breaks on a character split across two tokens.
